question: The marked price of an article is ₹800. It is sold at two successive discounts of 24% and 15%, respectively. Find the selling price of the article.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the multiplying factor method for successive discounts:

SP = MP × (100 − 24)% × (100 − 15)%

SP = 800 × 76% × 85%

SP = 800 × (76 / 100) × (85 / 100) = 8 × 64.60 = 516.80

**∴ The correct answer is ₹516.80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹800

Successive discounts = 24% and 15%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − d₁ / 100) × (1 − d₂ / 100)

 
 
 

 
 

 
 MP

**Calculations:**

⇒ First discount = 24% of 800 = (24 / 100) × 800 = 192

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 800 − 192 = ₹608

⇒ Second discount = 15% of 608 = (15 / 100) × 608 = 91.20

⇒ Final Selling Price (SP) = 608 − 91.20 = ₹516.80

**∴ The correct answer is ₹516.80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equivalent Single Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the equivalent single discount is given by the formula: D = (a + b − ab / 100)%.

Relation Between CP and MP

When both profit and discount percentages are given, the ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price is: MP / CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%).

Successive Percentage Change

If an amount undergoes successive changes of x% and y%, the net percentage change is: Net % = (x + y + xy / 100)%. Negative values are used for discounts or decreases.
